lines: You left me forty-one seconds of your voice and I have played it three hundred times.
It is you asking whether I have seen your blue jacket, and saying you will pick up bread on the way home, and laughing at something off to the side that I will never know.
We always think the last thing will sound like the last thing.
It will be a speech, a slammed door, a rain-streaked window.
I have not found the jacket.
I have stopped looking for it, in the way you stop looking for a word you are afraid you already know.
Tonight I played it again, and at second thirty-three you say my name the way you always did, as if it were the start of a joke only the two of us were allowed to finish.
I held my breath for the rest of it.
The recording ends, and I whisper, "Yes?" to the quiet.
The quiet, being kind, does not answer.
